Population.evidence_source: All respondents described that they had felt distress after the suicide attempt and that the initial encounter at the hospital was emotionally difficult. Respondents who were conscious at the time of admission to hospital as well as patients who were not (but awoke later) described having this reaction when they were admitted irrespective of when they regained consciousness. Some respondents were shocked over the fact that they had actually tried to kill themselves. For others, having survived was unexpected and painful. The respondents often experienced shame immediately after the suicide attempt and during the first encounters with the hospital personnel. One said that it felt like having taken off all his clothes, and the other respondent said that she felt like a bird that had had its feathers plucked.

Area.evidence_source: All respondents described that they had felt distress after the suicide attempt and that the initial encounter at the hospital was emotionally difficult. The respondents often experienced shame immediately after the suicide attempt and during the first encounters with the hospital personnel. Several patients described that their feelings of shame were alleviated, diminished, or were made more bearable when they were treated with kindness and respect. The feelings of shame were replaced by feelings of relief that they had received help.
